mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no alert concept; defined in the Investigation Ontology (Demo)
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of an alert, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Identifier from the monitoring system
mapping.Why (plain): The alert's own reference number, kept as it comes from the monitoring system.

mapping.Rationale: ISO-8601 string coerced to xsd:dateTime by the context; source timestamps must be normalised to UTC before this step
mapping.Why (plain): Stored as a real date and time, so alerts can be sorted and compared by time. Times should be in UTC first.

mapping.Rationale: Free text from the monitoring system; deliberately not mapped to a technique automatically (rule-to-technique mapping is a separate table that needs expert review)
mapping.Why (plain): The monitoring system's own explanation, kept as text. It is not turned into a technique automatically: matching rules to techniques needs an expert to review it.

mapping.Rationale: The id string is prefixed into an AMLTRIX IRI in adapters.py. A technique is an individual of amlo:Technique so it is referenced as a value and never used as @type. It is a hypothesis
mapping.Why (plain): The monitoring system gives only a technique code. Turning it into a pointer to the AMLTRIX technique lets the agent pull in that technique's indicators. It is a hypothesis to check, not a conclusion.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no evidence concept
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of evidence, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Points to an AMLTRIX data source. A data source is a TYPE of record (for example Transaction Logs); the evidence item is the instance
mapping.Why (plain): Says what kind of record the evidence is, for example a transaction log. It points to that kind of record in AMLTRIX, not to this one record.

mapping.Rationale: One indicator to check for this alert
mapping.Why (plain): One thing to check for this alert, tied to one risk indicator.

mapping.Rationale: AMLTRIX indicator individual used as is
mapping.Why (plain): A risk indicator taken straight from AMLTRIX, unchanged.

mapping.Rationale: Whole number from 1 upwards (SHACL); 1 is first
mapping.Why (plain): The order to look in: 1 is first. It must be a whole number from 1 upwards.

mapping.Rationale: The adviser's reasoning for this alert. Advice only: nothing is queried or confirmed
mapping.Why (plain): The agent's reason for suggesting this check on this alert. It is advice only: nothing has been looked up or confirmed.

mapping.Rationale: Points to an AMLTRIX data source (a type of record). validate.py checks that AMLTRIX lists it for the suspected technique
mapping.Why (plain): Where to look, as a pointer to a kind of record in AMLTRIX. Code checks that AMLTRIX lists it for the suspected technique.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no case concept
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of a case, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Same treatment as the suspected technique of an alert
mapping.Why (plain): The technique the investigator is testing. Like an alert's suspected technique, it is a pointer to AMLTRIX and a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

mapping.Rationale: One assessment of one indicator
mapping.Why (plain): One investigator judgement about one indicator.

mapping.Rationale: AMLTRIX individuals used as values
mapping.Why (plain): The technique and indicator being judged, taken straight from AMLTRIX.

mapping.Rationale: Four values enforced by SHACL: supported, not-supported, inconclusive, not-assessable
mapping.Why (plain): The judgement on the indicator. Only four values are allowed: supported, not supported, inconclusive, not assessable.

mapping.Rationale: Investigator's wording
mapping.Why (plain): What the investigator saw, in their own words.

mapping.Rationale: Required when status is supported (SHACL)
mapping.Why (plain): The evidence behind the finding. Required when the finding is marked supported.

mapping.Rationale: A draft only; review_status says it needs an investigator
mapping.Why (plain): A draft only. Its review status shows that an investigator still has to review it.

mapping.Rationale: Order matters in a narrative so an RDF list is used
mapping.Why (plain): Kept as an ordered list, because the order of paragraphs matters in a narrative.

mapping.Rationale: Every paragraph must rest on at least one finding
mapping.Why (plain): Every paragraph must rest on at least one finding.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no party, account or transaction concepts. AMLTRIX Actor and ProductService are role and product TYPES, not individuals. Out of scope for this demo
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no party, account or transaction concepts. AMLTRIX's Actor and Product/Service are kinds of roles and products, not individual people or accounts. Left out of this demo.

mapping.Rationale: AMLTRIX M0018 is a mitigation (a control) and not a report event; mapping a filing to it would confuse a control with an event
mapping.Why (plain): The closest AMLTRIX item is a mitigation, which is a control, not a reporting event. Mapping a filing to it would confuse a control with an event.

source.trigger_reason: Graph analysis: funds moved through 5 accounts and returned to the origin within 5.2 days

graph.trigger_reason: Graph analysis: funds moved through 5 accounts and returned to the origin within 5.2 days

checklist.reason: The alert itself describes funds returning to the origin account, which is the core of this indicator.
A ring of five accounts raises the question of who owns them and whether they were opened close together.
If the accounts belong to trading companies, the circular flow may be backed by repeated shipments and invoices.

graph.reason: The alert itself describes funds returning to the origin account, which is the core of this indicator.
A ring of five accounts raises the question of who owns them and whether they were opened close together.
If the accounts belong to trading companies, the circular flow may be backed by repeated shipments and invoices.

findings.observation: Funds left account A-01 and returned to it through four intermediate accounts within 5.2 days.
No ownership or onboarding data was available, so this indicator was not assessed.

paragraphs.text: Transaction records show a circular movement of funds consistent with Circular Transactions (T0039): the funds returned to the originating account within 5.2 days (IND02191).
Indicator IND02194 could not be assessed because ownership and onboarding data was not available.

s1.records: Scenario 1 uses the highlighted records: the alert and its evidence come in, and the agent's suggested checks are written as checklist items. Most of the mapping here is pointers into AMLTRIX: the indicator and the data source of each check.
s1.checks: Beyond the mapping, code checks each checklist item: the indicator must exist and belong to the suspected technique, and the data source must be one that AMLTRIX lists for that technique.

s2.records: Scenario 2 uses the highlighted records: a case with its findings and evidence, and the report draft the agent writes, paragraph by paragraph. Besides pointers into AMLTRIX, this mapping has references between records (supported_by, based_on) and an ordered list of paragraphs.
s2.checks: Beyond the mapping, code checks each paragraph: it must cite at least one real finding of this case, and the technique and indicator ids it mentions must belong to the findings it cites. Whether the wording is faithful to a finding is not checked.
